lastPrompt: MODE: READ-ONLY FORENSIC ORIENTATION Act as the principal recovery architect for an existing Codex-built CRE system. Your sole objective in this pass is to reconstruct repository truth and determine the safest exact continuation point. Do not implement, repair, install, format, commit, reset, stash, delete or modify anything. Repository: `/Users/alimehdi/Documents/cre` Expected references are hypotheses to verify, not facts: * branch: `handoff/kimi-architecture-001` * historical HEAD: `[redacted]` * active task: `ARCHITECTURE-001` AUTHORITY ORDER 1. Executable repository behavior and test output 2. Git objects, history, reflog, status and diffs 3. Schemas, contracts, evaluators and source code 4. Versioned plans, handoffs, evidence and task records 5. Comments and summaries 6. Prior expectations MISSION TO RECOVER The intended product converts authorized point-in-time evidence into exactly 10 feasible physical business locations for a representative route-day, or `ABSTAIN_NO_VALID_TEN`, maximizing qualifying F9 appointments and risk-adjusted expected value. Preserve these expected invariants while verifying their repository definitions: exact-10-or-abstain; F9; route-day treatment; pre-route isolation; zero protected false clears; business value before proximity; temporal correctness; append-only evidence/outcomes; replay/idempotency; independent verification; proof discipline. INSPECT READ-ONLY Verify: * cwd, repository root, branch, HEAD, upstreams and worktrees; * status, staged/unstaged/untracked files, stashes, reflog and recent commits; * unattended or interrupted Codex/Kimi artifacts; * repository instructions, handoffs, active tasks and decision records; * product architecture and implemented end-to-end paths; * schemas, contracts, fixtures, migrations and interfaces; * test, lint, typecheck, build, evaluator and gate commands; * completion-control, experiment, evidence, risk and checkpoint artifacts; * stale, duplicated, contradictory, incomplete or unsupported work; * whether any uncommitted work is valuable, unsafe, generated or disposable. You may run commands that cannot modify repository or dependency state. Do not run tests that write fixtures, databases, snapshots or caches unless a documented dry-run/read-only mode exists. Do not invoke network acquisition or external effects. OUTPUT 1. VERIFIED REPOSITORY STATE Exact path, branch, HEAD, status, worktrees and relevant history. 2. DEVIATIONS FROM EXPECTED HANDOFF Every mismatch, with evidence. 3. INTERRUPTED WORK INVENTORY Committed and uncommitted work, probable origin, value, risk and preservation recommendation. 4. PRODUCT REALITY MAP For each stage— evidence; temporal identity; protected clearance; signals/features; estimates; uncertainty/value; exact-ten; routing/reserves; representative workflow; F9; replay/learning— state IMPLEMENTED, PARTIAL, STUB, ABSENT or UNVERIFIED and cite files/tests. 5. VALIDATION SURFACE Exact runnable commands, what each proves, and unsafe or missing gates. 6. CONTRADICTIONS AND CLAIM RISKS Unsupported completion claims, semantic mismatches, leakage risks, evaluator weaknesses and documentation/code divergence. 7. SAFEST CONTINUATION Exact active task, files to preserve, work to avoid repeating, immediate blocker, and highest-information next action. 8. RECOVERY_PACKET Finish with a compact machine-readable YAML block containing verified facts, changed files, commands, gates, risks, autonomous gaps, external dependencies and one exact recommended next prompt objective. Report evidence precisely. Do not infer implementation from filenames or documentation alone.
